title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: normal basis of cargo release at destination by document type
content:
## Scope

At the destination end, each Bills of Lading and Transport Documents type has a normal basis on which cargo is released. This comparison table states that basis for every type, the number of originals that must be surrendered at destination for a normal release, and whether the surrendered original or eBL must carry an unbroken endorsement chain to the releasing party.

## Comparison table

| Document type | Normal basis of release at destination | Originals surrendered at destination for a normal release | Unbroken endorsement chain to the releasing party required |
|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Sea Waybill | Identification of the named consignee | 0 | No |
| AHL Electronic Bill of Lading | Surrender of the eBL record on the platform | 1 | Yes |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | Surrender of an original at the destination office | 1 | No |
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | Surrender of an original at the destination office | 1 | Yes |
| AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading | Surrender of an original at the destination office | 1 | Yes |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | Surrender of an original at the destination office | 1 | Yes |

## Grouped reading

- **Waybill:** the AHL Sea Waybill needs no original at destination; its normal basis is identification, and no endorsement chain applies.
- **Electronic record:** the AHL Electronic Bill of Lading releases on surrender of its single electronic record, which must carry an unbroken endorsement chain.
- **Paper sets:** the four paper types release on surrender of 1 original at the destination office. Of these, only the AHL Straight Bill of Lading, which is not negotiable, carries no endorsement-chain requirement.

## Points of judgement

**How many originals of an AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading are surrendered at destination for a normal release?** 1 original.

**Does the endorsement setting apply to an AHL Straight Bill of Lading?** No; its setting is No.
